source_title: Superpowers: A Composable Skills-Based Workflow System for Coding Agents

concepts.label: subagent-driven development
concepts.description: A method where a main AI coordinator spawns separate, fresh AI workers (subagents) to handle individual coding tasks, then reviews their output before moving on.
concepts.why_innovative: It breaks the common failure mode of a single AI losing track over long sessions by isolating each task to a clean, focused worker — enabling hours of autonomous, on-track coding without human babysitting.
concepts.impact_on_applications: This could let developers hand off a full feature request to an AI and walk away, returning to find a tested, reviewed, and organized implementation — dramatically reducing the time humans spend supervising AI coding tools like Cursor or GitHub Copilot.

concepts.label: composable agent skills
concepts.description: A library of reusable, self-contained instruction modules (called 'skills') that an AI agent automatically picks up and applies at the right moment during a coding workflow, without the user needing to ask.
concepts.why_innovative: Instead of prompting an AI differently every time or relying on its default behavior, skills provide reliable, repeatable processes — making AI behavior predictable and extensible like software plugins.
concepts.impact_on_applications: This could make AI coding assistants behave consistently and professionally across projects — the way a well-trained team member follows established best practices — rather than improvising unpredictably each session.

concepts.label: two-stage agent review
concepts.description: A quality-checking process where AI-written code is reviewed twice in sequence: first to check it matches the original plan, then to check it meets general code quality standards.
concepts.why_innovative: Separating 'did it do what was asked?' from 'did it do it well?' catches two distinct classes of mistakes that a single review pass often misses, raising the reliability of autonomous AI output.
concepts.impact_on_applications: This could reduce the number of bugs and design mismatches that slip through when AI tools write code automatically, making AI-generated software safer to deploy in real products without exhaustive human re-checking.

concepts.label: spec-first brainstorming workflow
concepts.description: A structured conversation process where the AI asks clarifying questions and builds a written specification (a clear description of what to build) before writing a single line of code.
concepts.why_innovative: Most AI coding tools dive straight into writing code, leading to solutions that solve the wrong problem; anchoring the entire session to an agreed-upon spec dramatically reduces wasted work.
concepts.impact_on_applications: This could save developers hours of back-and-forth corrections by ensuring an AI coding tool truly understands the goal upfront — similar to how a good contractor confirms blueprints before breaking ground.

concepts.label: enforced red-green-refactor
concepts.description: A strict rule built into the AI's workflow that forces it to write a failing test first, then write only enough code to make that test pass, before cleaning up — deleting any code written out of order.
concepts.why_innovative: AI agents tend to skip testing or write tests after the fact as an afterthought; making test-first development a hard constraint rather than a suggestion produces more reliable, verifiable code automatically.
concepts.impact_on_applications: Software built by AI tools using this approach would come with meaningful, trustworthy tests by default — reducing the hidden technical debt (future maintenance burden) that currently accumulates when AI writes untested code.

concepts.label: git worktree task isolation
concepts.description: A technique where each coding task is given its own separate, clean copy of the codebase (a 'worktree') so changes don't interfere with each other or the main project.
concepts.why_innovative: Running multiple AI agents simultaneously on the same codebase normally causes conflicts; worktree isolation allows true parallel AI development without those collisions.
concepts.impact_on_applications: This could allow AI coding tools to work on multiple features or bug fixes at the same time in parallel, cutting development time significantly for teams using AI-assisted workflows.
